Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading.

About the team + role

Our mission is to democratize finance for all. At Robinhood, we’re building an exceptional team that’s using frontier technology to tackle some of the world’s most important financial challenges. We’re looking for bold thinkers, sharp problem-solvers, and builders who want to make a real impact. This is a place where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. - Take proactive ownership of creative systems and processes, identifying opportunities to modernize and scale output
- Champion visual craft and quality across high-impact product launches

title: Product Designer II
description:
About Bestow

Life insurance is one of the world's most important products. It's also one of the hardest to build, distribute, and modernize. Bestow exists to change that.

Bestow is a leading vertical technology platform serving some of the largest and most innovative life insurers. Our platform unifies the fragmented, legacy value chain, enabling carriers to launch products in weeks instead of years. Carriers choose us to scale and operate at unprecedented speed, powered by AI and automation.

Bestow isn't selling policies. We're building the infrastructure that helps an entire industry move faster, reach more people, and deliver on its promise.

Backed by leading investors (Goldman Sachs, Hedosophia, NEA, Valar, 8VC) and trusted by major carriers, Bestow is powered by a team that moves with precision, purpose, and heart. If you want to help reimagine a centuries-old industry with lasting impact, join us.

Bestow offers flexible remote/hybrid work, meaningful benefits, equity, and substantial growth opportunities.

Bestow uses E-Verify to confirm the employment eligibility of all newly hired employees. To learn more about E-Verify, including your rights and responsibilities, please visit E-Verify.gov.

About The Team

The Bestow Product organization is responsible for defining, designing, and delivering exceptional digital experiences that solve real problems. Our team collaborates across Engineering, Revenue, and Ops to transform ideas into intuitive, valuable solutions that delight our users. We believe in evidence-based decision making and maintaining a relentless focus on customer outcomes to drive product excellence.

You will join the Underwriting module — the team shaping how underwriters and managers work inside the Bestow workbench: case management, capacity and workload, analytics, and the AI-enabled experiences that make complex insurance decisions faster and more trustworthy. This is operational, B2B product design in a regulated domain — dense workflows, high stakes, and real users who depend on clarity under pressure.

You will report to the Senior Manager, UX Design. This role is open to Remote (US). 

About The Role

Bestow is seeking a Product Designer II to join our Underwriting module's mission of making insurance more accessible and human-centered. You'll own design for key workbench initiatives — turning complex underwriting and manager workflows into experiences that are clear, efficient, and defensible.

We're looking for a designer who combines strong research instincts with the ability to shape and ship ideas quickly. The most meaningful work on this team happens where ambiguity is high: discovery starts before requirements are fully baked, and the best designers here don't wait for a finished PRD — they help define the problem, test direction, and bring partners along with evidence.

We’re seeking a passionate, hands-on, and comprehensive thinking Product Designer to join our kick-ass team at HP. We are looking for creative thinkers who are entrepreneurial, critical of the current experiences around them, and innovators who are energized to re-imagine the way people, brands, and services interact to make devices, services, and the overall HP brand more personal and valuable for everyone involved.

description:

About the Role
We are seeking a Product Experience Designer to help design intuitive, scalable digital experiences for complex enterprise applications and internal business tools. This role is ideal for a designer who enjoys solving challenging workflow problems, collaborating with cross-functional teams, and creating user-centered experiences that improve productivity and efficiency.

title: Product Designer
description:
You'll own features end to end, from a fuzzy concept to a shipped, polished experience, and you'll design the interaction paradigms for a product where AI is the medium, not a feature bolted on. This is a hands-on generalist role with a high degree of autonomy and a high bar for craft.

It's deliberately not built for hyper-specialists or managers. At Luma, AI is how the work gets done: you're expected to think, generate, prototype, and build with it, using AI coding tools to make real working features rather than static mockups. It fits someone who has already changed how they design around AI and can move fast through ambiguity. If you need clear direction handed to you or prefer to stay in mockups, this won't suit.

What You'll Own



- Lead major features end to end, from product thinking and user exploration to pixel-perfect visual design and high-fidelity interactive prototypes.
- Design and prototype fluid, novel interactions for a new medium, making complex AI concepts feel intuitive.
- Build functional prototypes and shippable features using AI coding tools, in close partnership with engineering.
- Hold an exceptionally high bar for craft across visual design, interaction, and prototyping.
- Drive work forward through ambiguity: step into problems early, decide with incomplete information, and keep momentum.
- Collaborate with engineers, product, and AI researchers to shape strategy and ship the design vision at quality.

First 90 Days

One way the first 90 could unfold.



- Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Learn the product and its AI-native interactions, and identify where the experience can be sharper.
- Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Own a real feature from concept to shipped, prototyped and built with AI tooling alongside engineering.
- Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Raise the craft bar around you and set patterns other designers and engineers can build on.

What You Bring



- 5+ years building delightful, innovative products at scale.
- Strength in both craft and product thinking, across visual and interaction design.
- AI woven visibly into your process and portfolio, with experience building functional prototypes in tools like Cursor or Claude Code.
- A portfolio of work that shipped to production, showing how you framed the problem, how it evolved, and its impact.
- Comfort moving fast, converging, and knowing when to stop iterating.
- A track record of creating momentum and influencing decisions across teams.
- A portfolio is required.

Nice to Have



- Experience designing complex creative software: video or photo editors, design tools, or developer tools.
- World-class interaction design: fluid micro-interactions, complex state transitions, prototypes well beyond static screens.

title: Product Designer, Amazon Music Product Design
description:
Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

title: Product Designer, Amazon Music Product Design
description:
Description

As a Product Designer on the Amazon Music Core Experiences Design team, you will design voice-first and multimodal interactions that shape how customers experience music through spoken language. You'll work at the intersection of visual craft and conversational design — crafting TTS responses, anticipating how customers interpret single and multi-turn voice interactions, and ensuring spoken experiences pair seamlessly with on-screen content across Alexa-enabled devices.

Working alongside senior product designers, product managers, engineers, and researchers, you will support the design of voice interactions that feel natural, useful, and delightful. You'll use your knowledge of conversational UX and visual design to build, iterate, and refine solutions with guidance from your team. To succeed, you need a passion for language, empathy for how people listen and respond, strong visual sensibilities, and the curiosity to explore how voice and screen work together.

Key job responsibilities



-  Design voice interactions and TTS response flows that are clear, natural, and contextually appropriate for Amazon Music customers
-  Create conversational wireframes, sample dialog scripts, response mapping documents, and flow diagrams to communicate design intent
-  Iterate on single-turn and multi-turn voice interaction patterns, anticipating how customers will interpret and respond to spoken prompts
-  Collaborate with design, product, engineering, and research teams to incorporate customer feedback, technical constraints, and usability findings into designs
-  Leverage existing templates and design systems to produce high-fidelity mockups for multimodal voice+screen experiences
-  Partner with cross-functional teams to ensure voice responses align with broader platform patterns
-  Present design work to partners and stakeholders for review and feedback
-  Contribute to language model training data and sample dialog interactions under guidance from senior designers

A day in the life

You'll start your day reviewing how a new TTS response sounds and reads on an Echo Show — does it feel rushed? Is the information hierarchy right when paired with the visual card? You'll sketch out a multi-turn flow for a new music request pattern, thinking through what happens when a customer says "no, not that one." You'll pair with your PM to walk through edge cases, sync with an engineer on what's technically feasible for response latency, and bring your work to a design crit where the team helps you refine the conversational cadence. You'll end the day documenting your iteration in Figma and noting open questions for research.

Amazon Music is an immersive audio entertainment service that deepens connections between fans, artists, and creators. Tono Health
Tono is pioneering the future of specialty medicine, starting with dermatology. Our AI-native platform connects a national network of medical and cosmetic dermatology specialists with the patients who need them. We subspecialize in oncodermatology, Hidradenitis Suppurativa, and chronic inflammatory disease, hair restoration, and skin of color, and we're laying the foundation for space dermatology. About The Role

We're looking for a product designer who wants to operate like a founder.

Not someone who waits for tickets or perfect requirements. Someone who sees opportunities, prototypes fast, shapes product direction, and ships experiences that move the company forward.

This is not a "make the UI pretty" role. You'll work across product thinking, interaction design, systems, prototyping, and execution. In many cases, you'll go from idea → prototype → shipped product in days, not quarters.

The best people for this role think strategically, build relentlessly, and use AI as leverage.

Why This Role Is Different

The role of design is changing.

AI has collapsed the distance between idea and execution. The best designers today don't just create mockups, they can explore product directions, prototype interactions, generate working interfaces, and pressure-test ideas themselves.

We Believe The Future Belongs To Designers Who



- Think like product leaders
- Prototype like engineers
- Use AI tools fluently
- Care about outcomes, not deliverables
- Move from ambiguity to shipped product with very little overhead

If that excites you, you'll probably love working here.

- Own product areas end-to-end, from initial insight to shipped experience
- Lead greenfield explorations and turn blank-canvas ideas into real products
- Prototype aggressively, in code, AI tools, Figma, or whatever gets the idea across fastest
- Work directly with engineers and PMs to shape product direction, not just execution
- Think deeply about systems, workflows, and how features compound across the platform
- Use AI tools as part of your daily workflow to increase speed, creativity, and iteration velocity
- Raise the quality bar across the company through strong product judgment and craft
- Push ideas into reality quickly instead of over-optimizing in planning phases

How We Work



- We optimize for speed of learning and iteration
- We prototype early instead of debating endlessly
- We use AI heavily across design, product thinking, research, and engineering
- We believe small, high-agency teams can outperform much larger organizations
- We believe the best builders in the AI era are token maxxers, people who use AI relentlessly to compress execution cycles, test ideas faster, and expand the scope of what a single person can accomplish
- We care more about shipping and learning than rigid role boundaries

What We're Looking For



- 3–6 years of product design experience, ideally at startups or highly product-driven teams
- A strong track record of owning products or features from concept through launch
- High agency. You naturally move things forward without waiting for direction
- Strong product instincts and clear opinions about what should exist and why
- Excellent visual and interaction design skills, grounded in systems thinking

title: Product Designer
description:
Compensation: $160k–190k base + meaningful equity

About Flint

The best education anyone has ever received is one person paying close attention to one student: moving at their pace, noticing what they missed, asking the next question at the right moment. But the current system is built around a compromise with one teacher managing thirty students.

Flint exists to take that compromise off the table. Personalized learning, at the scale of a whole school — every student working with something closer to a tutor, and every teacher able to see what's actually happening across their class instead of guessing.

Go look at the product before you read any further: app.flintk12.com

The Role

Students want something that stays with them, going at their pace and helps them get unstuck without just handing over the answer. Teachers want that happening inside a class they still control, and they'd like their evenings back. Admins want proof that the platform they rolled out is leading to teacher productivity and student progress.

Your job is to dive deep into this design problem, holding three sets of needs within one product. We’ll trust you to ship designs that are the best possible solution to our users most urgent pain points. tl;dr you'll get to own how Flint works and how it feels.

How We Work



- We move fast, and closely. You'll work with a small, senior team: one Product Lead, a Chief of Staff (Product), a CTO, and five engineers. We also have a running joke that we can’t keep up with our #product_updates channel because of how much we ship.
- Fast and good aren't in tension here. In our experience the fastest route to something good is getting a rough version in front of a real teacher early, which tends to be quicker than getting it right in private. Decisions with the highest impact have often happened within days, not month long sprints.
- We’re always learning. Call it on-brand or a bit on the nose, but learning from each other, our customers, the market have been key to our growth. We even have channels dedicated to sharing our workflow mistakes and wins. Education is also still being actively shaped as a field, and staying tuned to what users and the industry are telling us matters more than assuming we already know.
- Users drive our decisions. Our team isn't exclusively made up of former teachers, and that's deliberate. We'd rather build from real user feedback and a range of perspectives than from any one person's classroom experience. Our close connection with teachers, students, and admins helps us quickly understand what's working and what isn't.
- We design with AI, not around it. Lo-fi concepts out of Claude, prototypes we can put in front of a teacher the same week, PRDs drafted from screenshots and voice notes: these are just a few ways we’ve used AI to support our work, and it's a real part of why our loop is as short as it is.

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.

Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. title: Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

What you'll do



- Design and build products from concept through launch.
- Work closely with design and engineering on new features and launches.
- You care about the details—typography, layout, motion, responsiveness, loading states, and performance—that make an experience great.
- Contribute visual assets for marketing.
- Prototype ideas quickly using Figma, Claude, Cursor, and whatever tools helps move the work forward.

You might be a fit if



- You have 2–5 years of experience designing and building for the web.
- You move fluidly across the full design process, from early concept through final production.
- You have an instinct for the details that make interfaces feel considered: type, spacing, motion, and how they all work together.
- You know enough HTML and CSS to work effectively with engineers—or to build parts of the experience yourself.
- You're comfortable using tools like Claude

description:

About SyntheticFi

SyntheticFi is a fast-growing FinTech startup redefining the securities-backed lending world. We partner via B2B channels with Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs). Through our product, clients of RIAs are able to access the SPX box spread market, an institutional source of liquidity.

We are leveling the lending playing field between individual investors and very large financial institutions. On the SPX box spread market, our users can borrow money to buy a house or a car at the same interest rate as financial institutions borrowing hundreds of millions of dollars.

Since launch in early 2025, we have consistently seen 20%+ month-over-month growth. We have earned the trust of hundreds of RIA firms to manage over $2 billions in regulatory AUM through the SPX box spread market.

Who are we looking for?

As our Founding Product Designer, you will work directly with the Co-Founders of the company and have broad scope across both Product and UX design.

You need to have a strong Product sense. We do not have PMs, so you will work with our Product Engineers to set product direction together. You should be someone who asks sharp questions to understand user workflows and business logic, and identifies what truly needs to be solved before jumping into design. You can expect to spend a good chunk of talking to users to understand and solve for their needs.

You also need to have strong UI / UX skills. Our product has both B2B and B2C elements and requires a high degree of polish to meet the demanding taste of consumers. Under the hood, our product is one of the most complex financial products that retail investors have ever seen. Since we are the category leader, many of the UI / UX problems do not have a clear parallel in the industry for pattern matching. We expect you to push the envelope and set the standard here.

- Be the first Product Designer in a product with strong PMF. Get a front row seat to see how the rocket ship takes off.

- Benefits: 100% paid employee health plans + employer-funded 401(k) match

Product Designer at Lumion
Location: In-office, South Jordan, Utah Comp: Salary, meaningful equity, and bonuses tied to company revenue


What Lumion does
Lumion is the all-in-one operating system for trade and technical schools. We power the entire institution: AI-driven lead generation and conversion, enrollment, financial aid, student lifecycle management, and tuition payments. Most schools are still stitching together five or six disconnected tools to do what our platform handles.


America has a massive skilled trades shortage and the schools that train electricians, welders, and nurses are the bottleneck. We're backed by TTV Capital and Tusk Venture Partners.
Why this role matters


You would be Lumion's first dedicated product designer. Until now, design has been done by the founders, product managers, and engineers. That carried us a long way, and it is no longer enough.


Our engineers build with AI-native workflows, so the constraint on the product is no longer how fast we can write code. It is how fast we can figure out exactly what to build and make it excellent. That is design work, and right now it is our bottleneck.


The people who use our platform are admissions directors, school owners, and finance staff who live in it all day, and students making one of the bigger financial decisions of their lives. Most software in this industry was built a decade ago and looks like it. You get to set the bar for what great looks like in this market.


The work
You will own design across the entire platform.


Product design end to end. You take features from PRD to shipped: user flows, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and specs engineers can build from without guessing. You will work directly with the CEO and CTO in design sessions and own the outcome.


Prototypes. Before engineering commits to a build, we want a working prototype in front of real schools. You will produce clickable, testable prototypes fast and use what you learn to sharpen the spec before a line of production code gets written.


The design system. The platform spans lead management, enrollment, messaging, scheduling, payments, and reporting, and it grew fast. You will build the component library and interaction patterns that make it feel like one product, and that let engineers ship good UI without a designer in the room.


AI interfaces. Schools use Lumion to configure and supervise AI agents that text, email, and call prospective students. Designing how a non-technical admissions director sets up an agent, reviews its conversations, and learns to trust it is new territory with little prior art. You will define those patterns.


Student surfaces. Enrollment applications, document signing, and tuition payments, mostly on a phone. These flows handle real money and real decisions, and they have to be effortless.

title: Product Designer I
description:
ICON is hiring a UX professional to own the user experience for a core product area within BuildOS - our software platform used by architects, builders, and construction operators. In this role, you will lead end-to-end UX work for tools that connect users to ICON's construction technology, from discovery research through design handoff. You will run customer interviews, map complex workflows, build prototypes, test them with real users, and write specs that engineering can build from. You will work alongside engineers, product leadership, and internal and external customers to shape what gets built and why. This role is based at ICON's Austin, TX office and reports to the Director of Product.


RESPONSIBILITIES:
Discovery and Research: Run regular interviews with architects, engineers, and builders to learn their workflows, pain points, and unmet needs. Document assumptions, evidence gaps, and research priorities for your product area. Turn findings into clear insights that shape the roadmap.
Workflow Mapping and UX Design: Map user workflows and edge cases for complex, multi-step construction and design processes. Design for a range of users, from technical specialists to first-time operators with different levels of software fluency. Define data needs, integration points, and error states.
Wireframes and Prototypes: Create wireframes, interaction flows, and interactive prototypes in Figma or a similar tool. Deliver designs that are functional, polished, and clear.
Prototyping and Usability Testing: Build and test prototypes with target users on a regular cadence. Run lightweight usability tests and update designs based on real feedback. Check designs with engineering for technical feasibility before handoff.
Handoff and Engineering Collaboration: Deliver developer-ready specs with annotated designs, acceptance criteria, and interaction details. Work two or more sprints ahead of engineering so teams always have clear, well-defined work to pick up.
Cross-Functional Partnership: Collaborate daily with engineers, product leadership, and cross-functional partners. Present design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers in plain terms.
Strategic Alignment: Connect your design work to company-wide Objectives and Key Results (OKRs) so the user experience moves bigger goals forward.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

- 3+ in UX design, product design, or a similar role.
- A portfolio showing end-to-end design work — research through shipped product, not visual design alone.
- Experience running user interviews and turning qualitative research into design decisions.
- Strong fluency with Figma or a similar tool for wireframing, prototyping, and design systems.
- Experience designing for workflows with real constraints, not only consumer apps.
- Clear communication skills. You can explain design choices to engineers, leaders, and customers.
- Comfort working through ambiguity. You can define the problem, not just solve a defined one.

title: Junior Industrial Designer
description:
About ONO
At ONO, we design sleek, silent tools that help busy minds find a moment of clarity. Our flagship, the patented ONO Roller, is in the hands of more than 500,000 people worldwide, from overwhelmed students to design-obsessed professionals looking for a quieter way to focus.
We are a small, purpose-driven team that believes tactile tools can quietly support mental wellbeing. We move fast, execute with intent, and obsess over the details that make a product worth holding.


The Role
We are hiring a Junior Industrial Designer to help design the next generation of ONO products. You will work directly with our founder and own real deliverables, from first sketch to something we can put in front of a manufacturer. This is hands-on product design for someone who loves physical objects and understands what makes them tick: the click of a mechanism, the weight in your palm, the feel of a good detent.


This is an ongoing part-time, hourly role. We are looking for a designer who wants steady, flexible part-time work designing products that ship. Hours generally run 10 to 30 per week depending on what is in the pipeline.


You will get a Fusion 360 license and a direct line to the founder. You bring the portfolio, the modeling chops, and the instinct for how a product should function.


What You'll Own
Product Design & Development

- Design new fidget concepts, from rough sketches through refined, manufacturable 3D models.
- Model and iterate in Fusion 360, thinking through mechanisms, tolerances, and materials.
- Apply light engineering judgment so products feel right in the hand and hold up in production.
- Prototype, test, and refine based on how the object actually performs.
Packaging Design

- Design packaging that feels as considered as the product inside it.
- Prepare files and specs to hand off to print and manufacturing partners.
Trade Show & Physical Brand Presence

- Design our trade show booth and physical presence for events.
- Translate the ONO look into physical spaces, displays, and fixtures.
Graphic Design (as needed)

- Create graphic assets across product, packaging, and brand as projects require.
Concept Communication

- Present and communicate concepts clearly through sketches, renders, and short decks.
- Walk the founder and partners through your thinking so decisions move quickly.


What You Bring

- Portfolio: physical product design work, ideally toys, gadgets, or everyday-carry objects, showing both form and function.
- Fusion 360: working proficiency, including modeling for manufacture.
- Product instinct: a real feel for how things work, not just how they look.
- Sketching: strong hand skills and the ability to explain ideas visually.
- Communication: comfort presenting concepts and talking through tradeoffs.
- Independence: enough experience to own a design and make sound calls with light supervision.
- Part-time reliability: you keep work moving on a flexible schedule and flag blockers early.

- Set and hold the visual bar, establishing what good looks like and advocating for it across the product.
- Shape how new features look before they're built, bringing a visual perspective to early concepting.

First 90 Days

- Days 1–30 — Immerse & Diagnose: Audit the product's visual quality and map where it falls short and what the design system needs.
- Days 30–60 — Ship & Validate: Elevate a high-visibility surface and stand up the first version of the systematized visual language in Figma.
- Days 60–90 — Scale & Systemize: Build the live, interactive design system the team uses when shipping new features.

What You Bring



- 7+ years in visual and UI design, with a portfolio showing exceptional craft across typography, color, layout, and interaction.
- Systems thinking: you turn a strong visual language into a scalable, consistent foundation.
- Experience building or significantly contributing to a design system a team actually uses.

- A clear point of view you can articulate, and a portfolio of work that shipped and improved product quality.

About Agora Intelligence (d.b.a. Tilt)
Agora Intelligence is building the audited methodology layer agents call before touching portfolios. Our product, Tilt, is GitHub for rules-based investment methodologies: an open platform and marketplace where investment strategies are created, tested, audited, and distributed — by humans and AI agents alike. As AI agents begin managing real portfolios, they need a trusted source of verified investment logic before they can act. Tilt is that source.
We operate across two connected surfaces: InvestOS, an open standard that lets any brokerage or platform plug verified methodology into its own AI experience; and Tilt, the reference implementation of InvestOS. Tilt is an agentic harness where investors, portfolio managers, and creators can author, remix, and publish strategies. We're a small, senior team (from BlackRock, Bloomberg, BGI, and Quant Funds) backed by Portage Ventures, Lerer Hippeau, Cumberland Investments (and more), working with major brokerages and financial data providers.


What We're Building
InvestOS — an open standard for rules-based methodologies and its reference implementation.
We believe any idea — a theme, a trend, a thesis — can be turned into an investable view. On Tilt, anyone can express a view as a rules-based basket of assets in seconds, backed by evidence and scored against what actually happens. Whether you're modeling a thematic strategy, tracking an emerging technology, or capturing the public-market footprint of a private company, what used to take an index committee months now takes an API call — 100× faster, at a fraction of the cost. We also transform views found on the open web, into rules-based strategies. This lets us measure the performance of any opinion or prediction about the future. The unit is a tilt: a creator-authored view of the world.


The bigger bet: as AI agents take on more of investing, they'll need an open, trusted standard for how investment views are expressed, verified, and combined. When anyone can generate a strategy in seconds, the strategies aren't the asset. The system that versions, tests, and grades them is. We're building that standard — and the platform where those views are made. We’re also building the learning loops for when views resolve against reality, as measured by markets.

We're a team of ~25 senior-to-principal engineers, designers and AI/ML researchers. More than half the team are former founders. We move fast, challenge assumptions, and believe AI should fundamentally change how financial products are built. title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Nuvo

Nuvo is building the infrastructure that powers trade in the physical goods economy.

Every part of modern life depends on physical goods: the food we eat, the fabric we wear, the steel and concrete that shape our cities. Behind it all are 50 million businesses trading $100 trillion each year.

Consider how housing gets built. One company cuts down trees, another turns the wood into building materials, another sells the product wholesale, and a contractor uses them to build homes. Each step is a business trading with another to turn raw materials into finished goods.

Most of these businesses still operate through offline networks, held together by fragmented systems, manual processes, and institutional memory. When trade is slow, costly, or error-prone, the effects cascade — resources get misallocated, businesses can’t grow, and consumers face higher costs and fewer choices.

Nuvo builds technology that makes trade fast, automated, and intelligent. More than 75,000 businesses already use our platform, and we’re backed by $45M from Sequoia, Spark, Founders Fund, and Index as we build the operating system for global commerce.

The Role

Design at Nuvo sits at the center of how our platform works and feels. Our products span identity, risk, payments, AI, and more, all built on top of the connectivity between businesses on our platform. As a Senior Product Designer, you’ll shape how this system comes to life for thousands of businesses, defining how complex operations become simple, intuitive, and powerful.

You’ll operate with deep ownership, collaborating closely with engineering, product, and customer teams. You’ll help define the next generation of experiences that make Nuvo increasingly compelling across new industries and use cases.

What You’ll Do



- Drive design for major product areas that serve thousands of businesses
- Partner with engineers to build progressively and deliver high-quality results at speed
- Develop and scale our design language and system across surfaces and products
- Engage with customers to uncover insights and design from first principles
- Help define the design team’s culture, identity, and creative standards

Who You Are



- You gain deep context to set a high standard for what gets built, how, and why
- You learn quickly, connect patterns across identity, payments, and data, and use that understanding to shape product direction
- You collaborate with engineers, PMs, and other stakeholders, making thoughtful trade-offs, relaying context, and being a clear voice of the customer
- Have 5+ years in industry shipping high-impact products to solve complex problems

Expected Compensation Range $180,000-$250,000

- Founding design role — you define the standard, not inherit someone else's

- Comfortable with 0 → 1 ambiguity: you can start from a blank canvas and make confident decisions

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
The Opportunity:
We are seeking a Senior Product Designer to define the user experience for AI-powered procurement platforms. You will design intuitive interfaces that enable employees to interact with intelligent workflows, transforming complex business processes into guided digital experiences.


What You Will Do
● Product & Interface Strategy: Architect user journeys for complex, end-to-end enterprise applications. Own the UX for major platform features and ensure intuitive, error-resistant experiences.
● Frontend-Aligned Design: Design responsive, highly interactive, and accessible user interfaces. Partner closely with engineers to create technically feasible and scalable solutions.
● Information Architecture: Design robust workflows and navigation structures for high-volume enterprise data, making information easy to consume and act upon.
● AI Interaction Design: Create Human-in-the-Loop experiences for AI-powered features. Design interfaces that help users review, understand, and trust AI-generated recommendations and insights.
● Systems Thinking: Maintain and evolve enterprise design systems, ensuring consistency across platforms and seamless integration of AI-assisted workflows.
● AI-Assisted Design: Leverage modern AI design tools to accelerate ideation, asset generation, and design exploration while focusing on strategy, research, and problem-solving.


Requirements & Tooling
● Design Tools: Advanced expertise in Figma, including prototyping and design system management.
● Frontend Literacy: Strong understanding of React and TypeScript capabilities to create developer-ready designs.
● AI UX Frameworks: Experience designing for AI/LLM interactions, including user feedback loops, transparency, latency handling, and trust-building patterns.
● Prototyping: Experience with Protopie, Framer, or advanced Figma prototyping.
● Testing: Experience conducting usability testing and iterating on enterprise products based on user feedback.


What We’re Looking For
● Experience: 5+ years of Product Design experience within B2B SaaS, FinTech, enterprise software, or complex internal platforms.
● Architecture Focus: Ability to simplify complex data structures and multi-step workflows into intuitive user experiences.
● Collaborative Mindset: Strong partnership with engineering teams to deliver scalable, accessible, and user-centric solutions

Sycle is a market-leading global SaaS company with the mission of facilitating the delivery of better hearing to the world. Founded in 2001, we have grown to be the leading practice management solution for audiology (hearing care) providers, with more than 65% market share. The Sycle practice management solution frees up valuable time so our customers can grow their businesses through delivering high quality patient care and exceptional services that delight their customers. Small hearing care practices and some of the largest retailers utilize our software in 13 countries worldwide.

The Sycle team is 120 strong. We are headquartered in Lone Tree, Colorado with a large remote workforce across the US and Canada. We are seeking an experienced Product Manager – Clinic Analytics & Reporting to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of our enterprise reporting, business intelligence, and practice analytics features.This role will be based either in Denver or on the US West Coast.

title: Brand Designer
description:
About Us

Conversion is the agentic marketing automation platform for modern enterprises such as Plaid, ClickHouse, Webflow, and Productboard. Our platform lets growth teams run their entire go-to-market motion in one place, from acquisition through retention, with AI agents doing the work that legacy tools like Marketo, HubSpot, and Pardot can't.

We've raised $28M+ from Abstract Ventures, True Ventures, and HOF Capital. The team is based in San Francisco and includes engineers, designers, and operators from Airbnb, Palantir, Pinterest, IMC, Shopify, LinkedIn, and Microsoft.

About The Role

Hey 👋 Kyle here. I run product and growth at Conversion, and up until now I've also been the person holding our brand. Every logo lockup, every deck, every launch page, every color and type call. I've loved doing it. It's also the thing I most need to hand off, and the hardest for me to let go of.

So, now I'm hiring a brand designer. Someone who owns our visual identity top to bottom and builds the system the rest of the company designs against.

That means you're the person who decides what Conversion looks like and feels like everywhere it shows up. The identity system (logo, type, color, grid, motion language), the guidelines that keep it consistent, and the craft bar that everything gets held to. You'll bring it to life across web, social, launch creative, decks, and collateral. When we ship a new feature or run a launch, you're making the page look incredible, cutting the launch video, and setting the visual story. This is brand and identity work, not product UI (Levi owns our in-app surfaces), and not code. If you think of yourself as a design engineer, this probably isn't your seat.

I care about this a lot, which is why the bar is high. Portfolio first, always. I want to see identity work you've built from the ground up and can walk me through: what the problem was, what you made, why every decision. I'd rather see one brand you shaped end to end than ten logos you touched. Tool fluency is table stakes (Figma, Illustrator, After Effects / Lottie / Figma Motion, Claude Design), and I'm looking for roughly 1 to 5 years of doing exactly this.

The people who crush this role tend to be the same off the clock. Side projects, an art Instagram, a vlog, a brand they built just because. Strong opinions about advertising and what good creative actually is (I keep a Super Bowl ad tier list, so no judgment). The friend whose dinner party has a custom menu. Obsessive about craft down to the pixel. If that's you, and you want to own a brand rather than execute someone else's, this is a rare one.

This role is in-person 5 days/week in San Francisco.

What You'll Own



- The visual identity itself: logo, type, color, grid, motion language, and the guidelines that keep all of it consistent as more people build on top of it
- The look and feel of Conversion everywhere it shows up: web, social, decks, collateral, launch creative
- Launch work end to end: the launch

Selara is hiring a Staff Product Designer to work on VA.gov, the digital front door for the Department of Veterans Affairs. title: Director of Product Design
description:
FMX builds and delivers software through small, embedded product trios: a PM, a designer, and two engineers, each owning a suite of products end-to-end. We're hiring a Director of Product Design to own design strategy across the company, lead our design team, and stay hands-on in delivery.

This is a player/coach role. On the player side, you'll own the design work for one product-suite trio, shaping and validating solutions with customers through AI-accelerated design and high-fidelity concept builds. On the coach side, you'll set the vision and quality bar for design across every product suite, grow and develop the team, steward the design system, and partner with Product and Engineering leadership to make design a driver of business outcomes. The balance leans toward leadership, but you stay hands-on. Protecting that split, and protecting your team's focus, is part of the job.

Team & Charter Context: 



- Where you sit: Embedded as the designer in one product-suite trio (assignment finalized during onboarding), while leading the design function
- Who you lead: Three Product Designers plus one User Researcher shared across all trios, with room to add designers and managers as the team grows. You allocate the shared researcher deliberately and level-load designers across suites that run on different cadences
- How the org is structured: Suite-based trios, each owning products that serve similar customer outcomes across the full tier ladder
- Where you fit: You report to the VP of Product and sit alongside Product and Engineering leadership. Design leadership has been missing from that picture until now, and you'll define what it looks like

How We Work: 



- We validate solutions early with customers using high-fidelity concept builds: interactive prototypes, coded prototypes, and hybrid approaches
- Designers partner side-by-side with engineers ("concept builders") during concept creation. Ideation, interaction design, prompt-driven exploration, and iteration happen together, rather than through a handoff
- Delivery runs as a continuous flow. Work gets pulled by capacity, discovery happens alongside delivery, and a designer and engineer can shape and validate a concept the same day it comes up
- Cycles move fast: concept, test, learn, iterate

Responsibilities:

As the Director of Product Design, you will:

Do the work (embedded designer)



- Own the design work for one product-suite trio: frame problems, map user flows, and design and validate solutions with customers
- Use AI-powered design and prototyping tools to explore workflows and UI patterns quickly, and co-build coded prototypes with engineers to test with users
- Run rapid, formative usability tests on concept builds and drive iteration before delivery

Set design strategy



- Own the design vision across all product suites and align it with the company's product and business strategy
- Define what good looks like for FMX design, and build the roadmap to raise design maturit

PactFi provides secure, end-to-end, operational infrastructure for managing complex private credit transactions. Our web-based application brings together all parties involved in such a transaction to more efficiently allocate capital, complete KYC, share documents, manage funds flow, and more. PactFi was developed in close partnership with two of the industry's largest players, both of whom represent the top 3 players in the private credit space by both size (AUM) and deal activity.

The Design Problem



- Product is moving from a screen-first build model, where the underlying system is designed first and the interface follows.

- Permissioning is layered — participants often have their own downstream stakeholders who need visibility into a subset of the same information.

- Work closely with the PM and engineers on your surface to develop the strategy and rationale behind what you build, not just execute a spec.

description:

Device Brand Studio, an internal agency within the Devices group at Amazon, is seeking a talented Brand Designer to help bring new Amazon offerings to market, products, services, and features within our devices portfolio. -  Prepare and organize design files and assets for handoff to production and other teams
-  Contribute ideas and point of view in creative reviews, while executing to the direction set by leads
-  Manage time and priorities across multiple concurrent design requests

-  Have an available online portfolio
-  Experience working with agile development teams (agile/scrum/kanban)

-  Experience with e-commerce, search, social, and other major application types and their UX patterns

description:
About 9amHealth

9amHealth is an AI-enabled virtual specialty care platform focused on managing high-cost chronic conditions at scale. The company partners with employers, health plans, and pharmacy benefit managers to deliver comprehensive, cost-effective medical care for individuals living with obesity, diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia. Members receive access to specialized clinicians, including endocrinologists, obesity medicine specialists, and clinical pharmacists, at-home lab testing, prescription medications, and lifestyle support.

9amHealth was founded in 2021 and is backed by leading healthcare investors like Define Ventures, SemperVirens, 7Wire Ventures, and The Cigna Group Ventures.

About The Role

We’re hiring a Senior Product Designer to own 9amHealth’s consumer app — the daily touchpoint for people managing diabetes, blood pressure, cholesterol, or weight. This is a craft-led, senior IC role. You’ll design what our members see, what they tap, and how the experience responds. The quality of what you ship matters as much as the thinking behind it.

The mandate is broad and the canvas is genuinely open. Several tracks in the 9amHealth member experience are still largely untouched: mental health support, movement, and more. You’ll put your fingerprint on labs, medications, virtual visits, education, nutrition, tracking, and the onboarding and re-engagement patterns that tie them together. For an ambitious senior designer who wants to shape a product from the ground up, that scope is rare.

Our members carry real clinical risk,including vulnerability to disordered eating patterns. That means no unnecessary pressure, no calorie scolding, no shame loops. Holding “engaging” and “clinically safe” in tension at the same time is the real design challenge here, and the thing that makes this role genuinely hard and genuinely interesting. It’s also the part that no tool can do for you,it requires judgment.

The member app is also tightly integrated with our EMR, which we built ourselves. Clinical data surfaces on the consumer side. Member actions trigger Care Team workflows. A “message your Care Team” button has a queue behind it. A surfaced lab value is the tip of a workflow. You’ll work primarily on the consumer surface, but you need to think across that seam, because your decisions shape the clinical team’s day.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to our Head of Design. You’ll work day-to-day with a full product squad: a product manager, front-end and back-end engineers, and QA. Our product and engineering team is distributed across San Diego, (CA) and Vienna (AU), and this role is based in EST for maximum overlap with both.

What you'll do



- Own the companion app end to end: flows, surfaces, interaction patterns, visual system. Craft and quality are your accountability.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
In the 1960s, the Italian artist and inventor Bruno Munari was studying spontaneous forms: shapes that emerge from the interaction of material, function, and environment.

When Danese Milano commissioned him to design a lamp that was practical, durable, affordable, and easy to transport, Munari was reminded of the traditional rice paper lanterns he had encountered when traveling in Japan. But rice paper lanterns are fragile, hard to clean, and tend to yellow over time.

Looking for an industrial alternative, he discovered filanca—a synthetic stretch nylon used exclusively for women's stockings at the time.

Munari visited hosiery factories to test the material and see what forms it could take. "We do not make lamps, sir. Only stockings," one factory told him. Munari replied, "You'll see."

The result was the Falkland lamp: only a few centimeters thick when packaged, as tall as a human when hung, its spontaneous form emerging from the elasticity of the nylon and metal rings of different diameters inserted at regular intervals, enlarged by gravity when suspended from above.

Munari didn't begin with the form of a lamp. He began with the qualities it needed, then looked outside the conventions of lighting to find the right materials and methods. We're looking for a designer who works the same way: someone who studies the systems and materials at hand, then finds a way of putting them together that feels both unexpected and inevitable.

At Co–Star, the materials are a 4,000-year-old system of astrology, planetary data from NASA, and a corpus written by astrologers and poets. The qualities we're designing for: astrology made accessible without asking anyone to learn a complex system, and a language that lets people share something intimate with their friends.

We're hiring a Senior Product Designer to continue cultivating those qualities across Co–Star and new experiments. You'll move between product architecture, interaction design, prototyping, and visual design. Ideas rarely arrive as polished specs. You'll help decide what we make next and how it works.

title: UX Designer, AI App

About A1
There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks that are not AI-native. Our mission is to build a proactive smart assistant for everyday users to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal prompting.
Our product focuses on achieving high reliability for long-running workflows, persistent context, and real-world task completion. The system must handle multi-step reasoning, interact with external tools, and remain reliable despite non-deterministic model behavior. Our objective is to help users complete tasks daily enjoyable with over ~90%* reduced time.


Role
You will own the UX of A1's core app experience. This means designing the end-to-end flows users go through every day - how they start tasks, how they follow along as the AI works, how they stay in control, and how they recover when something goes wrong.
This is a UX role for a HCI product. You need to understand both user needs and AI system behavior well enough to design product flows that feel clear, reliable, and controllable.


What You'll Be Doing

- Own UX for A1's core app surfaces across iOS, Android, and web.
- Design complete user flows for AI-assisted tasks - from intent capture through to task completion, including handoff, progress tracking, and error recovery.
- Design how the app surfaces what the AI is doing, what decisions it has made, and what the user needs to confirm or adjust.
- Map and design the full range of AI states a user encounters - loading, thinking, acting, waiting, completing, stalling, failing, and recovering.
- Work with product, engineering, and ML teams to define user requirements and translate them into concrete design solutions.
- Conduct usability research to understand where users lose trust, feel uncertain, or disengage.
- Produce wireframes, user flows, and high-fidelity designs that engineering can build from directly.
- Contribute to the design system and shared UX patterns for AI app surfaces.
- Design for both simple everyday interactions and complex multi-step AI workflows within the same product.


What You Will Need

- Experience as a UX designer on consumer mobile or web apps, with a strong portfolio.
- Solid skills in user flow design, wireframing, and high-fidelity prototyping in Figma.
- Ability to design for systems that are asynchronous, non-deterministic, and context-dependent.
- Clear thinking about user trust, control, feedback, and transparency in AI-driven product experiences.
- Experience conducting user research and turning findings into design decisions.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving teams with evolving product scope.
- Ability to balance simple consumer UX with complex AI system behavior.
- Good judgment on usability, edge cases, failure handling, and recovery flows.

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About Revin

At Revin, our mission is to bring superintelligence to the built world. Millions of operators across Home Services, Construction, and Remodeling have been overlooked by the last wave of technology. We believe AI is the most transformational platform change in history, but the hard work lies in thoughtful, context-aware applications of this technology to the real world.

Revin provides operators with an end-to-end system of intelligence to automate and scale revenue. Our modular suite of products includes Scheduling, Appointment Management, Membership Management, Inside Sales, Revenue Capture, Marketing, and Funnel Optimization.

Today, over $3B in revenue runs on Revin, making us the number one AI partner for enterprise operators. Our customers include Sears Home Services ($800M), Astara Capital ($700M), Del Air ($150M), Long Home Remodeling ($150M), ImproveIt Remodeling ($100M), Sage Home ($80M), and more. We have raised $10M from top investors including Stellation Capital, 1Sharpe, Gokul Rajaram, Russ Heddleston, Michael Werner, Tandem, Max Branzburg, and Marc Bhargava.

About The Role

We are hiring our first in-house Senior Product Designer to own product design end-to-end: the dashboard where operators configure, monitor, and trust AI agents that handle revenue-critical conversations over SMS, voice, and email. When our agent gets something wrong, it can cost a customer real money, so much of the work is designing for trust. Our users run $100M+ businesses and are busy running them, not learning software, so your job is to make a genuinely complex AI system feel obvious.

This is a founding role: you will set the design foundation the rest of the company builds on, and work AI-natively to get there.

Why This Role

The honest pitch: we are handing the entire design surface of the company to one person, right before it gets much bigger.

The dashboard is yours. The design system is yours. The patterns that decide whether an operator trusts an AI agent with their revenue, yours. How Revin looks and feels in the market, yours. You will not be handed a style guide and a backlog. You will decide what good looks like here and then build it.

This is our first in-house design hire, and the ceiling is the design function itself. Do this well and you grow into leading design as we scale the team.

What You Will Do



- Own product outcomes end-to-end for the Revin dashboard, from problem framing through research, interaction design, high-fidelity UI, and design QA in production. What matters most is whether the experience genuinely works for customers
- Work as an equal partner to the product manager and engineers, shaping what to build together rather than taking specs and handing back mocks
- Make the agent trustworthy by design: show operators what it did and why, surface the evidence behind a decision, give them clear ways to review and override, and design a calm path for when it gets something wrong

Job Details

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. The world of work as we know it is changing and we're looking for Trailblazers who are passionate about bettering business and the world through AI, driving innovation, and keeping Salesforce's core values at the heart of it all.

Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Applications for this position will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

Design at Qualified is small and intentional. There's no design systems team or research ops function, just close access to the product, fast feedback loops, and problems that rarely have obvious solutions.

Most of those problems are about AI where the interface is rarely the hard part. The challenge is helping users understand what the AI is doing, trust it when it's right, catch it when it's wrong, and shape it toward what they actually need. That takes judgment more than process.

We’re building Piper, an AI SDR that runs autonomous sales conversations, follows up with prospects, and moves pipeline without a human in the loop. Piper is not a chatbot and not a copilot. Piper is an agent. You will work on two of its most interesting surfaces: the AI brain (how Piper understands prospects and explains its reasoning) and conversational presence (the live chat and video experience where the AI is the rep).

What you'll work on

The first surface is Piper’s brain: how Piper understands a lead, forms a plan, and explains its reasoning. You'll design the interface for shaping its personality, goals, and objection handling. Not a settings panel. Something closer to a thinking partner you can tune.

The second is Piper's live presence, the chat and video experience where the AI is the rep. The work is in the details: the micro-interactions, latency handling, turn-taking, and tone that make it feel credible instead of uncanny.

The design patterns for autonomous agents in enterprise sales are still being figured out. You'll be part of that.

How you work

Taste Over Process. Prototypes Over Presentations. Speed Is a Quality, Judgment Is The Craft. You Think Of Yourself As a Creative Director Of AI Collaborators, Not a Solo Craftsperson. Concretely

title: Staff Visual Designer - Design Systems
description:
In 1954, architect Eero Saarinen designed a radically modern bank branch for Irwin Union in Columbus, Indiana. With glass walls, no private offices, and a floor plan that invited openness, it embodied a new kind of transparency in finance. The building was surrounded by trees, furnished by Herman Miller, and featured rustic brick flooring. Today, that space is a conference center, and that spirit of design-forward thinking in banking feels all but extinct.

Mercury believes that level of care and craft in design has been lost in modern finance and we’re building a brand that brings it back. We're a financial technology company building products that feel extraordinary to use. We help people and businesses accomplish more with their money by turning banking* from a frustration into a catalyst for their ambitions.

Our Design Systems team sets the visual foundation that every product designer, every UI surface, and every expressive product moment builds on, from the foundations like type and color, to highly expressive brand-in-product moments that make Mercury feel considered.

We’re looking for a Staff Visual Designer to raise the ceiling on craft across Mercury’s design system and product experience. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can see the whole UI system and knows how to evolve it at scale.

Design Foundations is a brand-new team at Mercury, responsible for design systems, brand in product, and AI tools to help anyone build. This means this role has real agency to define it: supporting a highly collaborative team that’s hungry to grow its craft, and a clean slate for setting the vision forward.

In this role, you’ll:



- Redefine and ship large, foundational improvements to Mercury’s design language (things like type, color, and iconography) that scale beautifully across every product surface.
- Partner with Brand and other craft leaders to bring expressive moments into the product and set direction for how brand and product visual language work together.
- Set the craft bar for the design org: define what excellent looks like, and build the systems, guidelines, and references that make it repeatable.
- Actively coach product designers on their craft, giving direct feedback that raises the quality bar across both individual work and the design system itself.
- Partner with design systems designers and engineers to make sure visual decisions translate cleanly into scalable, maintainable components.
- Represent design systems and visual craft in conversations with Brand, Engineering, and design leadership.

What you’ll bring:



- 10+ years of experience in visual design, with deep expertise in typography, color systems, and iconography at a product or brand scale.
- A portfolio that shows range: foundational systems work as well as high-craft, expressive visual design.
- Not just taste, but conviction and language to articulate what makes something successful.

At its core, MEP is about building the technology backbone that enables a diverse set of internal stakeholders, from content and marketing teams to product and engineering, to leverage Netflix's messaging capabilities at scale, with the right guardrails and the right level of self-serve flexibility. You will develop a deep understanding of what each internal team needs, synthesize those inputs into a coherent platform strategy, and translate that strategy into a prioritized roadmap that reflects the highest-leverage opportunities across all stakeholders. title: Eyewear Designer
description:
At Pair Eyewear, we believe in placing our people at the center of everything we do. We are dedicated to fostering a joyful and dynamic workplace, providing our employees with an environment where they can thrive and make a meaningful impact.


Pair Eyewear is looking for a frame designer to own the look, feel, and design identity of our eyewear. This is a creative, concept-driven role: you’ll define the aesthetic direction of our frames and bring new shapes and collections to life through sketching, illustration, and hand-drawing. You’ll set the design vision and partner with our development team to take concepts toward production. If you have an eye for form, a point of view on style, and a love of eyewear, we want to see your work.


What You’ll Do:

- Define the look, feel, and design identity of Pair’s frames — from overall aesthetic direction to the details of each shape.
- Conceptualize and develop new frame designs through sketching, illustration, hand-drawing, and digital rendering.
- Explore form, proportion, silhouette, and style across the collection.
- Direct materials, color, and finish (CMF) — selecting and combining acetate, metal, and mixed materials to express each design.
- Develop balanced, on-trend collections aligned with the Pair brand and the product roadmap.
- Partner with the product development team to carry concepts from idea toward production, keeping the design intent intact.
- Research eyewear, fashion, and materials trends, and study competitor product, to keep the line fresh and distinct.
- Present design concepts and direction clearly to cross-functional partners.


Who You Are:

- A frame designer with a strong point of view on style, form, and what makes eyewear feel special.
- A skilled illustrator — confident in hand-drawing and digital sketching to communicate ideas quickly and beautifully.
- Trend-aware and curious, with a feel for where eyewear and fashion are heading.
- Organized and self-driven, able to run multiple designs in parallel against a product calendar.
- Collaborative — you enjoy working with development, category, and brand partners to bring designs to life.


Need to Have:

- Direct eyewear industry experience designing frames.
- Degree in Industrial Design, Product Design, Fashion Design, or a related field — design school strongly preferred. Equivalent professional experience considered.
- Strong hand-drawing, illustration, and digital sketching skills (e.g. Procreate, Photoshop, Illustrator).
- A strong sense of form, proportion, brand aesthetic, and color/material/finish.
- Working knowledge of eyewear materials and construction — enough to design with manufacturability in mind.
- A portfolio showing original eyewear / frame design, from concept through finished product.


Nice to Have:

- Experience designing for a direct-to-consumer/ wholesale retail or high-volume eyewear brand.
- Specialized eyewear-design training or apprenticeships.
- A background in trend or CMF research.

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. title: Knitwear Designer
description:
Rose Holding USA is the United States arm of Rose Group, a vertically integrated sweater and knitwear manufacturer based in Bangladesh. We manage design, development, and production programs for established brands including French Connection, Karl Lagerfeld, DKNY/Nautica, Margaritaville, and Chaps.
Our vertical structure means our designers work in direct partnership with the manufacturing team producing the garment — an uncommon degree of access in this market, and a meaningful advantage in both speed and product quality.
The Role
Reporting into the New York team, the Sweater Designer will own seasonal development from concept through production handoff:

- Develop seasonal sweater collections including sketches, CADs, colorways, and yarn and stitch direction
- Build stitch stories across cables, jacquard, intarsia, pointelle, links-links, and novelty textures
- Specify gauge, yarn count, and construction; author complete tech packs
- Translate market and runway trend research into commercially viable product for US buyers
- Present seasonal concept boards and line reviews to buyers
- Monitor competitor assortments, retail pricing, and emerging category trends
Working With Our Bangladesh Team
This role involves substantial, ongoing collaboration with our production and technical teams in Bangladesh. It is a core function of the position rather than a peripheral one:

- Daily communication with factory merchandisers, knitting technicians, and QA staff
- Review and approval of knit-downs, swatches, protos, and fit samples in partnership with the technical team
- Troubleshooting construction, gauge, and yarn issues directly with the mill and knitting floor
- Aligning design intent with production capability early in the calendar to protect margin and delivery
- Periodic travel to Bangladesh may be required for seasonal development and line reviews
Candidates should be comfortable operating across a nine-to-ten hour time difference and building working relationships with an overseas team. Bengali language ability is a plus but is not a requirement.
Qualifications

- 3+ years of dedicated sweater design experience across full-fashion and cut-and-sew
- Comprehensive knowledge of gauges (3gg–16gg), yarn types, and knit construction
- Proficiency in Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop; Shima Seiki or Stoll experience strongly preferred
- Demonstrated ability to read and correct knit-downs
- Prior experience working with overseas manufacturing partners
- A portfolio demonstrating both design sensibility and commercial judgment
Details

- Full-time, on-site at our New York City office
- Salary range: $60,000–$72,000 annually
- To apply, submit your resume and portfolio to arnob@roseholdingusa.com

title: Senior Product Designer
description:
About The Role

Artemis Security is hiring a Product Designer to shape how security teams actually use our platform. In cybersecurity, most tools are built by engineers for engineers, and it shows - dense UIs, buried workflows, and dashboards no one actually looks at. We're building something different: a platform that security teams reach for because it's genuinely well-designed, not just powerful.

You'll own the end-to-end product experience across the Artemis platform, from the earliest concept sketches through pixel-perfect execution. You'll partner directly with our founders, product, and engineering leadership on the decisions that shape how the product feels, flows, and gets used every day. This is a role for a designer who thrives in complexity: security work generates enormous volumes of information, and you'll need a strong command of visual hierarchy — knowing what to foreground, what to tuck away, and how to make dense, data-rich interfaces feel clear and navigable.

Just as important is connective thinking: designing intuitive links between different areas of the product so teams can move fluidly from signal to investigation to response without losing context. You'll design for a technical, high-stakes audience — CISOs, security architects, SOC analysts — where clarity and trust matter more than flourish.

- Own product design end to end for the Artemis platform, from research and discovery through interaction design, visual polish, and hand-off

- Build and evolve our design system so product velocity increases as we grow, without sacrificing quality or consistency
- Lead user research with security practitioners, from customer calls and shadowing sessions to structured usability testing
- Contribute to product strategy by bringing a strong point of view on what to build, not just how to build it
- Work closely with our brand and marketing designers to ensure the product experience feels like a natural extension of the Artemis brand

Qualifications



- 5+ years of product design experience at an enterprise SaaS company, with meaningful ownership of complex, workflow-heavy products
- A portfolio that demonstrates strong end-to-end product thinking, not just visual polish — clear examples of research, tradeoffs, and shipped work
- Experience designing for technical or expert users (developers, security teams, data teams, IT admins, or similar), where dense information and complex workflows are the norm
- Strong systems thinking, including experience building and scaling design systems across a growing product
- Fluency in Figma, and comfort collaborating in engineering-adjacent workflows (li

Adobe Design is looking for a Senior Designer to join the Document Cloud team, focused on Acrobat Mobile Growth. This role is for someone who thinks in systems and executes in details, who can hold the full shape of a mobile experience in their head while also caring deeply about a single moment of friction.

You will work across the Acrobat Mobile experience to understand how people discover, adopt, and build habits around the product, and to design the surfaces, flows, and patterns that make that journey coherent.
